'''Ram Charan Mehrotra''' (16 February 1922 – 11 July 2004) was an Indian analytical and organometallic chemist, academic, educationist and the vice chancellor of the Universities of [[Delhi University|Delhi]] and [[Allahabad University|Allahabad]].<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/deceaseddetail.php?id=N640447 | title=Deceased fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=5 November 2016 | archive-date=9 November 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109152807/http://insaindia.res.in/deceaseddetail.php?id=N640447 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was known for his studies on the chemical theory of indicators, alkoxides and carboxylates of many elements.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=300 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> He was an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Chemical Society]], [[Chemical Society of London]], [[Royal Institute of Chemistry]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="Deceased Honorary Fellows, Foreign Fellows and Fellows">{{cite web | url=http://nasi.nic.in/deceased.htm | title=Deceased Honorary Fellows, Foreign Fellows and Fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016}}</ref> and [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Mehrotra,_Prof._Ram_Charan | title=Fellow profile | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=5 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1965, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Rajasthan University Gate.JPG|thumb|[[Rajasthan University]]]]
Ram Charan Mehrotra was born in a middle-class family on 16 February 1922 in [[Kanpur]] in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]] to Ram Bharose Mehrotra, a small-time cloth merchant and his homemaker wife, Chameli Devi.<ref name="Publications2003">{{cite book|author=Europa Publications|title=The International Who's Who 2004|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sR4Ch1dMe8IC&pg=PA1120|year=2003|publisher=Psychology Press|isbn=978-1-85743-217-6|pages=1120–}}</ref> He lost both his parents before he turned 10 and had to continue his studies depending on merit scholarships and part-time jobs like private tuition.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/BM/BM28_0512.pdf | title=Ram Charan Mehrotra | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | work=Biography | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016}}</ref> His primary schooling was at Municipal School, Kanpur and later he joined Christ Church School (present-day [[Christ Church College, Kanpur]]) from where he passed the [[Pre-university course|intermediate course]], standing first in the state. Joining the [[University of Allahabad]] in 1939 for his graduate studies, he completed the course on the strength of three scholarships{{Refn|group=note|[[Amarnath Jha]], the then vice chancellor of the university, allotted two additional scholarships to Mehrotra}} and passed BSc with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry as optional subjects. He continued at the university for MSc in chemistry which he passed with first rank in 1943. During this period, he was also involved in student politics in connection with the [[Quit India Movement]] of 1942 and had to stay away from studies for four months.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" />

Before starting his formal academic career by joining Allahabad University in 1944 as a member of faculty of inorganic chemistry, Mehrotra worked at Vigyan Kala Bhawan, Daurala, a local learning centre involved in teaching science to prospective young entrepreneurs, for ten months during 1943–44 and was also associated with ''Vigyan Pragati'', a science magazine published by [[National Institute of Science Communication and Information Resources]] (NISCAIR) of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> He served the university till 1954; in between, he had a short stint of two years at [[Birkbeck College]] from 1950 to 1952 as a British Council Fellow and part-time faculty, working with [[Donald Charlton Bradley]]; he utilised this period to secure a PhD from the [[University of London]] in 1952. He returned to India the same year and resumed his service at Allahabad University when he was offered the position of a reader at [[Lucknow University]] in 1954. After serving four years there, he moved to [[Gorakhpur University]] in 1958 as a professor where, a year later, he was promoted as the dean of the faculty of science.<ref name="Publications2003" /> It was during this time, he served as a member of the Review Committee in Chemistry of the University Grants Commission of India under the chairmanship of [[T. R. Seshadri]], where his colleagues included [[Asima Chatterjee]], a noted chemist.<ref name="Review Committee in Chemistry">{{cite web | url=https://archive.org/stream/chemistryinindia032633mbp/chemistryinindia032633mbp_djvu.txt | title=Review Committee in Chemistry | publisher=Osmania University | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref>

In 1962, on invitation of [[Mohan Sinha Mehta]], the then vice chancellor of the [[University of Rajasthan]], he took up the post of a professor and head of the newly formed chemistry department and served the institution for two decades. In between, he had a five-year stint as the vice chancellor of [[Delhi University]] (from 1974 to 1979)<ref name="List of Vice‐Chancellors since 1922">{{cite web | url=http://uic.du.ac.in/images/2-%20List%20of%20Vice-Chancellors.pdf | title=List of Vice-Chancellors since 1922 | publisher=University Information Centre, Delhi University | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> and a short assignment as a [[University Grants Commission (India)|UGC]] National Fellow in December 1979 but on completion of those assignments, he returned to Rajasthan University, where he stayed till 1982; on his move from the university, he was made an emeritus professor. That year, he became associated with the activities of the [[University Grants Commission (India)|University Grants Commission]], first as the chairman of the Commission on Revision of Pay Scales to Teachers which submitted its report to UGC in 1986.<ref name="Government of India Notification On Revision of Pay Scale of Teachers">{{cite web | url=http://www.ugc.ac.in/oldpdf/psorders/1986.pdf | title=Government of India Notification On Revision of Pay Scale of Teachers | publisher=University Grants Commission | date=17 June 1987 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Background">{{cite web | url=http://www.ugc.ac.in/oldpdf/pub/report/4.pdf | title=Background | publisher=University Grants Commission | date=9 July 1987 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> Simultaneously, when the ''National Commission on Teachers'' was constituted by the Government of India in 1983 under the chairmanship of [[D. P. Chattopadhyaya]], he was appointed as a member of the Research Advisory Committee.<ref name="Research Advisory Committee">{{cite web | url=http://www.teindia.nic.in/mhrd/50yrsedu/r/2Q/42/2Q420101.htm | title=Research Advisory Committee | publisher=Government of India | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> After his assignment with the committee, he took up the chair of the Book Writing Project of the [[National Council of Educational Research and Training]] (NCERT) and in 1991, he was appointed as the vice chancellor of the University of Allahabad, a position he held in 1993.<ref name="Former vice chancellors">{{cite web | url=http://allduniv.ac.in/home/pages/136 | title=Former vice chancellors | publisher=Allahabad University | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref>

Mehrotra was married to Suman, a Hindi scholar, whom he married in 1944 around the same time when he joined Allahabad University. The couple had two daughters, Rashmi and Shalini and one son, Piyush Mehrotra, in between.<ref name="Publications2003" /> He died on 11 July 2004.

== Legacy ==

=== Researches ===
Mehrotra, during his early years in research, made notable contributions in analytical chemistry which included studies on tin, gold and hydrated copper
oxide.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> Through his researches on the chemical theory of indicators, he elucidated the applicability of universal type of indicators, ceramic salts and of hypobromites and widened the understanding of alkoxides and carboxylates of many elements.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34}}</ref> His work covered the synthesis of several metallic compounds such as polymetaphosphates, [[alkoxides]], beta-diketonates, [[carboxylates]], [[thiolates]] and dialkyl 1 [[dithiophosphate]]s.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

=== Academics ===
While serving Rajasthan University as a professor, Mehrotra was known to have contributed in organizing a research school there and successfully tried to obtain Special Assistance Program as well as University Leadership Program from UGC.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> The research school has since published several original research papers in international journals. Similarly, he established research schools on inorganic and [[organometallic]] chemistry at the universities of Allahabad, Lucknow, and Delhi.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> During 1971–72, as a UGC National Professor, he delivered lectures at many Indian universities and he was a pioneer in popularizing science through Hindi medium for which he was awarded a cash prize by the Government of India in 1985. Besides over 800 articles published in peer-reviewed international journals,<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Mehrotra=3ARam_Charan=3A=3A.html | title=Browse by Fellow | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | work=Publications by fellow | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} he authored five books viz. ''Metal alkoxides'',<ref name="BradleyMehrotra1978">{{cite book|author1=D. C. Bradley|author2=Ram Charan Mehrotra|author3=D. P. Gaur|title=Metal alkoxides|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b-_vAAAAMAAJ|year=1978|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=9780121242503 }}</ref> ''Metal [beta] [beta]-diketonates and Allied Derivatives'',<ref name="MehrotraBohra1978">{{cite book|author1=R. C. Mehrotra|author2=R. Bohra|author3=D. P. Gaur|title=Metal [beta] [beta]-diketonates and Allied Derivatives|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o7d2QwAACAAJ|year=1978|publisher=Academic Press}}</ref> ''Metal Carboxylates'',<ref name="MehrotraBohra1983">{{cite book|author1=Ram Charan Mehrotra|author2=R. Bohra|title=Metal Carboxylates|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r8NTAAAAMAAJ|date=January 1983|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-488160-0}}</ref> ''Alkoxo and Aryloxo Derivatives of Metals''<ref name="BradleyMehrotra2001">{{cite book|author1=Don Bradley|author2=R. C. Mehrotra|author3=Ian Rothwell, A. Singh|title=Alkoxo and Aryloxo Derivatives of Metals|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=noeJ0u7mOoIC|date=22 February 2001|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-08-048832-5}}</ref> and ''Organometallic Chemistry''.<ref name="Mehrotra2007">{{cite book|author=R. C. Mehrotra|title=Organometallic Chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NSQy3mFKRM8C|date=1 January 2007|publisher=New Age International|isbn=978-81-224-1258-1}}</ref> He has also prepared texts for [[Indira Gandhi National Open University]] as a member of the Block Preparation Team.<ref name="Author Block Preparation Team 1">{{cite web | url=http://www.egyankosh.ac.in/browse?type=author&value=Block++Preparation+Team+(+Prof.+Ramcharan+Mehrotra+and+Prof.+Deshmitra+Puri) | title=Author Block Preparation Team 1 | publisher=Indira Gandhi National Open University | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Author Block Preparation Team 2">{{cite web | url=http://www.egyankosh.ac.in/handle/123456789/23949/browse?type=author&order=ASC&rpp=20&value=Block+Preparation+Team+(+Prof.+Ramcharan+Mehrotra%2C+Prof.+S.A.A.+Jaedi%2C+Dr.+Anirudh+Singh+and+Prof.+T.S.Shrivastav) | title=Author Block Preparation Team 2 | publisher=Indira Gandhi National Open University | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref>

=== Administration ===
Mehrotra was involved in policy-making bodies from early stages of his career when he sat in the Review Committee in Chemistry in 1960 and the committee made a number of recommendations on improvement of curriculum, research environment, and examination procedures of chemistry education in India.<ref name="Review Committee in Chemistry" /> During 1963–67, he sat in the Chemical Advisory Committee of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India]].<ref name="Publications2003" /> The ''Commission on Revision of Pay Scales to Teachers'' which he chaired in 1983 recommended that the procedure for selection of teachers should also include an assessment of the physical and mental abilities of the candidates.<ref name="National Commission on Teachers (1983-'85)">{{cite web | url=http://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/bitstream/10603/35255/11/11_chapter2.pdf | title=National Commission on Teachers (1983-'85) | publisher=Shodh Ganga | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> The commission also recommended for pay scale revision of the teaching staff ranging from over 200 to more than 300 per cent which was subsequently accepted by the Government of India and the revision was implemented in 1987 with retrospective effective from 1 January 1986.<ref name="Government of India Notification On Revision of Pay Scale of Teachers" />

Mehrotra served as the president of the chemistry section of the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 1967, he would also serve as its national president in 1979.<ref name="List of Past General Presidents">{{cite web | url=http://sciencecongress.nic.in/html/past_general_presidents.php | title=List of Past General Presidents | publisher=Indian Science Congress Association | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605035323/http://www.sciencecongress.nic.in/html/past_general_presidents.php | archive-date=5 June 2016 }}</ref> Besides participating in the UGC ad-hoc commissions, he was also associated with the body as a convener of its chemistry panel and his association with the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) included the chair of the Chemical Research Committee (1975) and membership in CSIR Society and CSIR Governing Body (1963–66 and 1976–80).<ref name="Publications2003" /> He served as the president of the [[Indian Chemical Society]] (1976–77) and Vigyan Parishad, Allahabad, as the vice president of the Indian National Science Academy - INSA (1977–78) and as a member of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] (1977–81). He was also a member of the INSA council from 1979 to 1981.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
During his early years at Allahabad University, Basu received the E. G. Hill Memorial Prize of the university in 1949 for the best research work by a member of the science faculty.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> The Indian National Science Academy elected Basu as a fellow in 1964 and the University of London honored him with the degree of Doctor of Science in 1965. The ensuing years would see him receive several [[honoris causa]] doctorates from Indian universities viz. [[Meerut University]] (1976), [[Kanpur University]] (1996), [[Bundelkhand University|Jhansi University]] (2000) and [[Banares Hindu University]] (2000). The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1965.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> The [[Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry]] awarded him the FICCI Award for Science and Technology in 1975 and he received the Professor T. R. Seshadri Seventieth Birthday Commemoration Medal of the Indian National Science Academy in 1976<ref name="Professor T. R. Seshadri Seventieth Birthday Commemoration Medal">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#ptr | title=Professor T. R. Seshadri Seventieth Birthday Commemoration Medal | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016 | archive-date=16 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#ptr | url-status=dead }}</ref> and the P. C. Ray Award of the Indian Chemical Society in 1977. He was awarded the National Fellowship by the [[University Grants Commission (India)|University Grants Commission]] in 1980 and the Golden Jubilee Medal by the [[Institute of Science, Mumbai]] in 1984.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

The J. C. Ghosh Medal of the [[Indian Chemical Society]] reached Mehrotra in 1986, followed by the Academic Achievements Award of the [[Sōka University]] in 1987.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> The [[Indian Science Congress Association]] honored him with four awards; starting with the Platinum Jubilee Distinguished Service Award in 1988; followed by G. P. Chatterjee Award  in 1991, Acharya Narendra Dev Award in 1992 and Ashutosh Mukherjee Award in 1993. In between, he received the inaugural [[Atmaram Award]] of the [[Central Institute of Hindi]].<ref name="Atma Ram Award">{{cite web | url=http://khsindia.org/india/hi/?option=com_content&view=article&id=260:atmaram-award&catid=64:awards&Itemid=920&lang=en | title=Atma Ram Award | publisher=Central Institute of Hindi | date=2016 | access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Chemical Research Society of India]] awarded him Lifetime Achievement Award in 1999 and the Indian Chemical Society awarded him the Platinum Jubilee Award in 2000.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" /> He was an elected fellow of the Indian Academy of Sciences,<ref name="Fellow profile" /> Indian National Science Academy and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="Deceased Honorary Fellows, Foreign Fellows and Fellows" /> and a fellow of the [[Chemical Society of London]], [[Royal Institute of Chemistry]] and the [[Indian Chemical Society]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> He also delivered several award orations and featured lectures; Special lecture at the XVII International Conference on Coordination Chemistry (1977), Plenary lecture at the XIX International Conference on Coordination Chemistry (1978), Plenary lecture at the IV International Conference on Solute-Solvent Interaction (1978), Clarence Karcher Memorial Lecture of [[University of Oklahoma]] (1982), the inaugural Foundation Lecture of the Federation of Asian Chemical Societies (1987) and N. R. Dhar Memorial Award Lecture of the National Academy of Science, India (1991) are some of the notable ones.<ref name="Ram Charan Mehrotra" />
